chapter: After high school: riverfront and tailoring
title: Palace Theater big bands and the Natchez fire
summary: He and friends heard big bands at the Palace Theater and Tick Tock, and he tells how a lack of money kept them from a Natchez show that burned.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, yes, because it was a style at the time. John McNeely, Charles Dimes, myself, Edward Johnson, we were all good friends. And we all would meet down on Rampart Street and we'd party at the Pelican or sometime we went to the Tick Tock. We used to go to the, see, then we'd go to the Palace Theater where all the big bands would come. And we had Savannah Churchill, where Red Fox, where, let's see who all would come down there. I'm just trying to think of one of them. Buddy Johnson played down there. Favorite piano player of mine. Andy Kirk with Claude Zajore. I'm trying to think of a piano player. Boy, the guy was fastest right hand I've ever seen in my life, I heard. Ken Kersey. Used to love to go to the Palace Theater. And then by that time I'm growing up, I'm finishing high school, getting ready to go to college, or either I'm in college, you know. And I could stay out a little late. I take advantage of being a young man because I'm working. Tell my mother, told a couple of little fibs to my mother, you know. So I went on down to the Palace Theater and that's where I started finding out about big time vans and about jazz, you know. Go to the Astoria. Let me tell you an odd thing that really happened. A fellow by the name of Harry Taylor, who was a cab driver in 1949, I think it was. And we all were supposed to go to see, what's his name was, it's on the tip of my tongue right now. They had a big thing, he used to play the Tick Tock all the time. And he had a big thing going on in Natchez, Mississippi. So, five or six of us got together and we were going to take a trip to Natchez, Mississippi to go see this particular band. I came up with my money, Harry Taylor had the automobile. Jim Dixon had his money, but the other two guys didn't have their money. So Harry say, I can't put my car on the road with just the three of us. There's not enough money to buy the gas and the food and stuff for us and then pay to go in. Well, to make a long story short, two days, it was a day later, we found out there was a big Natchez fire. And over 60% of the people who went to that doggone show got burned up. The Lord blessed us. And I'm alive today. I'll never forget that long as I live. Poor Harry Taylor, he's dead today.
